items.title: Randy Brecker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 12, 2022
items.q: I saw, when I was starting to do this Truman Capote was interviewed, the great writer on one of the talk shows.

ctx.x: I wanted to ask you, you mentioned when you were trying to articulate that thing you said yeah I can’t even do this anymore. I wondered if at the time — it’s a two part question. First of all the rhythms of the melodies and the whole band, did you have to spend a lot of time figuring out how to notate those things? Was it a chore? [Scats]

Well it was a craft that’s the way I looked at it. And once again it came from an interview. I saw, when I was starting to do this Truman Capote was interviewed, the great writer on one of the talk shows. And he was — I’m always interested in other artists’ thought process or work process. And he spent a little time in his interview talking about just the craft of writing books, writing literature. The fact that you just have to sit down and do it every day. So it’s not — he didn’t wait for inspiration. And I…
Yeah. You’re not the only one.
